1.explanation:
All these files cover the pipeline that loads the HTML template, applies String.replace to inject JS/CSS, and renders the report: 

• report-generator-test.js & report/v2/report-generator-test.js verify how the file contents are inserted via replace
• formatter-test.js ensures the overall HTML scaffolding is correct
• handlebar-helpers-test.js exercises the escaping helpers used in the templates
• cards-partial-test.js & table-partial-test.js confirm how partial templates are rendered into the page

Reviewing these gives you the code paths where replace is used, the exact templates under test, and how unescaped “$” sequences could slip through to break the final HTML.
1.bug_scenario: When a developer injects custom JS into the generated report by passing the file’s contents as the replacement string to String.replace, any “$” sequences in that injection (e.g. console.log('$');) are treated as replace-patterns (like $' = rest of the original string). As a result, the injected code drags trailing HTML into the replacement, breaks out of the intended <pre> wrapper, and corrupts the report page’s structure. In the screenshot, you can see the <body> element truncated and stray script tags and text rendered in the page, proving the injection escaped and malformed the report.
